title: Ohm's Law: Voltage, Current, and Resistance

scenes.narration: Why does your phone charger get warm while fast-charging, or a ceiling fan slow down when voltage drops during summer in Bengaluru?

params.topic_en: Ohm's Law: Voltage, Current, and Resistance Ohm's Law V = I × R Electricity in everyday gadgets

scenes.narration: Compare water tanks: rooftop tank fills kitchen taps. Flow like cricket matches: one tank fills many taps. Table: train schedule, train, station, time.

params.topic_en: Ohm's Law: Voltage, Current, and Resistance Roof Tank Height → Voltage (V) Pipe Water Flow → Current (I) Narrow Tap → Resistance (R) Pressure pushes flow Narrower path restricts flow

scenes.narration: Georg Ohm discovered that Voltage equals Current multiplied by Resistance: V equals I times R. Doubling voltage doubles the current if resistance stays constant.

params.topic_en: Ohm's Law: Voltage, Current, and Resistance V = I × R V : Voltage (Volts) I : Current (Amperes) R : Resistance (Ohms Ω) I = V / R R = V / I

scenes.narration: Let's test a two hundred thirty volt Indian wall socket powering an iron box with forty-six ohms resistance. Two hundred thirty divided by forty-six gives five amperes of current.

params.topic_en: Ohm's Law: Voltage, Current, and Resistance Supply: V = 230 V Heater Coil: R = 46 Ω Formula: I = V / R Result: I = 5 A 230 V ÷ 46 Ω = 5 Amperes

scenes.narration: To recap: Voltage pushes electrons, Resistance opposes them, and Current is the resulting flow governed by V equals I times R.

steps: Resistance (R): Opposition to flow in Ohms (Ω)
Current (I = V / R): Flow rate in Amperes
params.topic_en: Ohm's Law: Voltage, Current, and Resistance Key Takeaways: Ohm's Law Voltage (V): Electrical pressure in Volts Resistance (R): Opposition to flow in Ohms (Ω) Current (I = V / R): Flow rate in Amperes
